resource_sampling.scope: test executable only; excludes runner/cargo and subprocesses
resource_sampling.thread_count: macOS ps -M thread rows; raw user/command fields discarded
resource_sampling.rss: ps rss KiB converted to bytes; low-frequency samples, not an exact peak

boundary: Microseconds; Core intake only, no renderer click latency. Exact success-only RPC quantiles and all-response counts remain separate; n=1 is one observation. Stage p95_upper_us is a histogram bucket bound. Fixed-rate completion/s is not maximum throughput. RSS/threads are sampled process-only peaks. A finite owner/slow-tool fixture cannot prove absence of sustained starvation or unobserved quota overflow.
limitations: One full matrix per revision; this is not a statistical reliability or p99 claim.
Core intake response only, not native click-to-paint.
No observed logical peak field; cap 50 is source and regression evidence, not measured matrix peak.
Cumulative DB queue wait, Stop p95, steady response maximum, CPU and RSS increased; see results report.
Finite owner fixtures do not prove absence of sustained starvation.
Fixed offered steady rate is not maximum throughput.
Rounds five and six are not complete.
50-way approval success counts match, but admitted owner identities differ across runs; success latencies are not fully paired by owner.
The 50-way approval and Stop cases do not drain naturally before cleanup; recovery yields final persisted terminal states.
One/ten/thirty-second slow-tool overlap isolation was also present in round three.
